note: Promise vs Delivery register for Housing Domain 10. A promise is set beside a result only when the pledge and the series share geography, period and unit. Every other pledge is listed with the reason it is not scored, and its match is null. Delivered values are never stored here; the UI computes them from the API using match. context_indicator_ids are context to show nearby, not a score. Statements are short quotations from official or manifesto text. Overlap between a pledge and a series is not evidence that the policy caused the result.

target.period_note: Each calendar year wholly inside the Parliament elected on the pledge (first met 31 October 1951, dissolved 6 May 1955). 1955 is left out because the Parliament ended in May.

pledges.measure_definition: Permanent houses and flats completed in Great Britain in a calendar year, all builders. The pledge itself defines nothing; this is the measure used in the Commons and Lords exchanges of 1951 and 1952. Great Britain is England + Wales + Scotland from ONS country tables; prefabs are excluded.
pledges.status_note: The target was first exceeded in 1953, and output peaked in 1954. A 1984 Commons remark dates the target to 1954, but that was the peak year.

sources.label: HM Treasury, Autumn Budget 2017 (HC 587), 22 November 2017

target.period_note: Exchange assumption: 'on track to reach' 300,000 is read as reaching it by 2025, the middle of the decade; the Budget gives no year. The verdict is the financial year 2024-25 (April 2024 to March 2025), the latest outturn ending in 2025. Earlier years from 2017-18 show the path.

pledges.measure_definition: Net additional dwellings in England (MHCLG Live Table 118), one financial year. The Budget's 2016-17 baseline of 217,000 matches the net additions figure published at the time; the Budget itself does not name the statistic.
pledges.status_note: The year 2025 is an assumption made here, not stated in the Budget. 2025-26 outturn is due in November 2026; MHCLG's interim estimate for that year is also below 300,000.

pledges.measure_definition: Affordable homes started on site with programme funding, Homes England (outside London) plus the GLA (London), summed over the five financial years 2021-22 to 2025-26. The 180,000 was conditional ('should economic conditions allow').
pledges.status_note: The headline was conditional and was replaced in July 2024 by a 110,000 to 130,000 range, including at least 40,000 for social rent. The NAO reported that agency targets totalled 157,000 at launch.

pledges.title: Right to Buy one-for-one replacement (2012)
pledges.made_by: Department for Communities and Local Government
pledges.statement: "every extra council property sold under the scheme will be replaced by a new affordable home for rent"

sources.label: DCLG press release, 120 councils sign up to keep Right to Buy cash (2 July 2012)
DCLG, Reinvigorating Right to Buy and one-for-one replacement: information for local authorities (March 2012)
MHCLG, Right to Buy sales and replacements, England: 2024 to 2025 (21 August 2025), Figure 7

target.period_note: From 2 April 2012. Each year compares replacements since April 2012 with additional sales up to three years earlier, as MHCLG measured it. Scored to March 2025: MHCLG stopped reporting the target after the Government response of 2 July 2025. Applies to additional sales above the pre-2012 baseline, not all sales.

pledges.measure_definition: Cumulative receipt-funded new-build starts and acquisitions since April 2012, divided by cumulative additional Right to Buy sales (above the pre-2012 baseline) up to three years earlier. MHCLG publishes both figures; the ratio is computed from them. 1 or more means the national target was met that year.
pledges.status_note: The Housing Act 1980 created the statutory right to buy. The 2012 pledge changed discounts and the use of receipts in England. From 2023-24 Homes England stopped separately recording receipt-funded starts, so replacements may be undercounted.

pledges.measure_definition: Purchases of new-build homes supported by a Help to Buy equity loan in England (MHCLG Help to Buy statistics).
pledges.not_scored_reason: Monthly Help to Buy completions are now in the registry (help-to-buy-equity-loan), and one completion is one buyer. The Budget does not say from which date 'another 135,000' is counted, so the period is undefined. Listed, not scored.
pledges.status_note: The 2013-2021 scheme was followed by a 2021-2023 scheme for first-time buyers only. The scheme closed on 31 May 2023; the November 2023 release is final.
